hook: The CMG helicase hands human PRIMPOL to the leading strand to restart stalled DNA replication.
summary: Using purified human proteins to rebuild a stalled replication fork, the authors show that PRIMPOL binds directly to the CMG helicase, which aims it at leading-strand priming and keeps the leftover DNA gaps small. A cryo-electron microscopy structure shows the contact, and breaking it abolishes restart in vitro and PRIMPOL-dependent damage tolerance in human cells. The reconstitution is simplified compared with a living cell.
title: Human replisomes direct a dedicated leading-strand primase for fork restart.
